findings.summary: Scorecards in pipeline-cli/src/usage/scorecard.ts take the model from the assignment log, which now holds the alias. When a task has no assignment entry, the model comes from the usage-majority fallback, which holds the versioned id from the transcripts. The same role can then show up as two rows, 'sonnet' and 'claude-sonnet-4-6', and the routing-bar evaluation only counts the alias row. This is a cosmetic split, not a failure. The task summary already notes that results before and after a release share a row, but it does not mention this split. Optional follow-up if cohorts look fragmented.

findings.summary: securityCellTooWeak is relative to the table's own strength order. With the built-in id 'claude-opus-4-6' absent (as in this table), the only requirement is that the security cell is the LAST strength entry, so a later main-branch edit that reorders or shrinks strength (e.g. [opus, sonnet] with security on sonnet, or [sonnet] alone) would still validate. This predates this PR (with the built-in id present, its index is equally table-defined) and requires a reviewed merge to main, so it is not exploitable via a PR. Consider an absolute anchor, e.g. a fixed list of acceptable security families or ids in code, so the floor does not depend on table-declared ordering. Under the table as written the security reviewer is pinned to opus: no candidates, exploration excluded, and overrides cannot apply to a top-of-strength cell.

findings.summary: Audit-precision tradeoff, not a security defect: with family aliases, emit-leaf --model, the assignment log and scorecards record 'sonnet'/'opus' rather than a version, so the exact model behind a past review cannot be recovered from the leaf. The leaf model field was always a free-text string the pipeline asserts about itself (not verified against the served model), so no integrity guarantee is lost. Optionally record the harness-reported resolved model id alongside the alias if version-level forensics matter.

A compliance.yaml holding a schema-valid ModelRouting (or UsageConfig) document used to fail with a clear 'Expected kind CompliancePosture' error; it now passes validation and fails at line 128 with a TypeError on spec.regimes. It still fails closed and I found no production caller; the same gap already exists for every other registered kind (AutonomyPolicy and so on). Suggest an explicit kind check in the loader.

findings.summary: Pre-existing and not introduced by this diff: `kind in SCHEMA_FILES` also matches inherited Object.prototype names (constructor, toString, __proto__). Such a document goes to validate()/getValidator(), which throws 'Schema not found'. loadConfig does not catch that error, so one file in the trusted config directory aborts the whole load instead of producing a warning. KIND_KEY is never reached with these names. The new ENVELOPE_ARTIFACT_KINDS check uses Set.has and is not affected. Suggest Object.hasOwn(SCHEMA_FILES, kind).
